messages:
keith: Ran an nsys capture on the canary pool to investigate a perf regression. Seeing repeated 100-300ms stalls between kernel launches when serving with KV cache enabled. CUPTI is spitting attach/flush errors intermittently, e.g. 'cuptiActivityFlush failed: 999' and 'CUDA driver/runtime version mismatch'.
anya: ugh. which nsys version and container image? also paste the CUPTI stack snippet if you can.
keith: command I used:
```
nsys profile --output=/tmp/nsys_run --trace=cuda,cudnn --sample=none --duration=60s 
  --target-processes=all --capture-range=cudaApiLaunch
```
error excerpt from nsys log:
```
[2026-02-12 17:03:12] CUPTI: cuptiActivityFlush failed (err=999)
[2026-02-12 17:03:12] CUPTI attach failed: drvApiGetVersion reported 530, libcuda reports 525
```
keith: container uses redwood-infer:canary-2026-02, host driver is 525.85, toolkit in image is 11.8/530 ABI.
olivia: that mismatch explains the CUPTI/flushing weirdness. nsys relies on matching driver/CUDA ABI. two paths: bump host driver to 530 series or run profiling with a tool that supports mixed ABIs (messy).
sam: are we sure the stalls are CUPTI-related and not our kernel-selection fallback hitting a slow codepath? timeline shows long idle then a long kernel right after = could be a fallback to the scalar kernel for kv-cache misses.
keith: good call. i inspected the timeline: after the usual fast matmul kernels we have ~150ms gap, then a big fallback kernel labeled matmul_fallback_fp16. That lines up with the stalls. BUT the gaps only appear when CUPTI attach fails in logs, so it's either skewed tracing or the runtime will choose a different kernel if tracing is attached?
anya: interesting: we had a prior bug where the runtime disabled the fast fused kernel if profiler hooks were present (we did a conservative fallback to avoid racey async kernels). maybe the CUPTI attach failing toggles a fallback flag.
infra-bot: noticed: k8s seccomp profile drops CAP_SYS_PTRACE in our profiling job template. That will cause CUPTI to try and attach and fail.
keith: tried running with --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE and mounting /tmp/.nv across host; CUPTI attaches cleanly, no attach errors, and the big gaps disappear in nsys timeline. latency back to baseline.
olivia: so root causes: (1) driver/CUDA ABI mismatch causing intermittent attach/flush errors, (2) our runtime toggles safe kernel selection when profiler hooks are present, and (3) default pod seccomp/caps prevent a clean attach.
sam: proposed short-term mitigations:
- add a health check in the profiler bootstrap: verify cuDriverGetVersion vs libcuda and warn if mismatch (log + telemetry),
- detect failed CUPTI attach and avoid flipping kernel selection flag (keep fast kernels),
- update profiling pod template to include CAP_SYS_PTRACE or recommend host-side trace runs.
keith: implemented quick guard in canary: REDWOOD_INFER_PROFILER_STRICT=1 to force no-kernel-fallback when attach fails. validated with a /proc/driver/nvidia/version check at startup.
monitor-bot: perf-alert: canary latency regression cleared after canary rollout (03:10 UTC) :thumbsup:
anya: follow-ups: file a small runbook for profiling (driver/tooling matrix + pod caps), and we should add an automated preflight that checks driver/toolkit ABI and seccomp caps before running nsys. i'll open a ticket.
keith: thanks all — i'll paste the short reproduce steps and the nsys timeline snippet into the ticket. quick repro steps:
1) run canary without CAP_SYS_PTRACE and with mismatched driver (host 525, image 530)
2) run nsys profile command above
3) observe CUPTI attach errors and matmul_fallback_fp16 gaps
workaround: run with CAP_SYS_PTRACE and match host driver or run nsys on host.
keith: cc @olivia @anya @sam — will draft the runbook and patch the profiler bootstrap check later today. :white_check_mark:
